rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In derived forms from رميت, Sībawayh gives رموية for an expected رميية to avoid successive yāʾs and kasra, as in the nisba رحوي from رحى.
rows.anchor: لو لم يكن بعدها شيء كانت كياء رحى في الاعتلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In patterns such as فعول and فعليل from رميت, the sequence is رميي; a quiescent wāw before yāʾ changes to yāʾ, while the first yāʾ remains.
rows.anchor: ولكنك قلبت الواو التي قبل الياء لأنها ساكنة وبعدها ياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For فعليل from غزوت, غزوي replaces the wāw with yāʾ after a quiescent yāʾ, paralleling فعيل such as غزي.
rows.anchor: غزوت غزوي تقلب الواو ياء لأن قبلها ياء ساكنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فعول from غزوت becomes غزوي: the form avoids three wāws together with the damma, as in other changed forms such as عتي and معدي.
rows.anchor: يستثقلون الواوين في عتي ومعدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مفعول from قويت is مقري, and فعول from قويت is قوي; both are altered on the model of forms from غزوت with several wāws.
rows.anchor: وتقول في مفعول من قويت هذا مكان مقري فيه لأنهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أفعولة from غزوت is أغزوة, with أدعوة and أدعية also attested; أفعول from قويت is أقوي and undergoes the same waw change as مفعول.
rows.anchor: من غزوت أغزوة وقد جاءت في الكلام أدعوة وقد تكون أدعية على أرض مسنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For فعلول from شويت and طويت, Sībawayh gives شووي and طووي, avoiding the yāʾ sequences that would result from turning both wāws into yāʾs.
rows.anchor: وتقول في فعلول من شويت وطويت شووي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The related pattern فيعول from طويت is طيوي; speakers who retain yāʾ sequences in forms such as أميي and حيي would instead say طيي.
rows.anchor: وقد قلبت الواوين طيي وقد اجتمع فيها مثل ما اجتمع في فعول وذلك قولك طيوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فيعلول from غزوت is غيزو, like مغزو; from قويت it is قيو, with the radical wāw changed but the added pattern wāw retained.
rows.anchor: بمنزلة مغزو وهي من قويت قيو قلبت الواو التي هي عين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In فيعل from حويت and قويت, the medial weak radical becomes yāʾ after a quiescent yāʾ and the final radical becomes alif after the preceding fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وتقول في فيعل من حويت وقويت حيا وقيا قلبت التي هي عين ياء للياء

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans analyze the pattern as فيعل with a kasra on the medial radical, claiming that this form is limited from its original shape.
rows.anchor: إلا فيعلا مكسور العين لأنهم يزعمون أنه فيعل

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil says فيعل and فيعل alternate when the weak wāw or yāʾ is the medial radical, just as the corresponding feminine plural patterns alternate when it is final.
rows.anchor: الخليل فكان يقول عاقبت فيعل فيعلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For قويت and حييت on فعلان, Sībawayh gives forms with two open wāws; these remain unassimilated because the vowels make them like sound roots.
rows.anchor: وتقول في فعلان من قويت قواوان وكذلك حييت فالواو الأولى كواو عور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other فعلان forms assimilate: قويت gives قوان and حييت gives حيان, by analogy with assimilation in فعلان from رددت.
rows.anchor: وتقول في فعلان من قويت قوان وكذلك فعلان من حييت حيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A speaker who says حيي عن بينة instead of assimilating says قووان in the parallel form.
rows.anchor: ومن قال حيي عن بينة قال قووان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form حيوان replaces a yāʾ with wāw to avoid an initial quiescent yāʾ beside another unchanged weak radical.
rows.anchor: وأما قولهم حيوان فإنهم كرهوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dialect forms differ: قويت may yield قويان, while speakers who lighten عمية or alter رية from رؤية give قووان or قيان.
rows.anchor: ومن قال عمية فأسكن قال قويان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فيعلان from حييت, قويت, and شويت gives حيان, قيان, and شيان by deleting a yāʾ, as in فيعل and the corresponding diminutive pattern.
rows.anchor: وتقول في فيعلان من حييت وقويت وشويت وحيان وشيان وقيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مفعلة and فعلوة from رميت are مرموة and رميوة; the first keeps wāw because the verb form رمو has the same vowel environment.
rows.anchor: رميت مرموة لأنك تقول في الفعل رمو الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فعلة from رميت and غزوت is رموة and غزوة when not built on a feminine form of فعل; when built on that pattern it is رمية and غزية.
rows.anchor: على فعل قلت رمية وغزية لأن مذكرهما رم وغز فهذا نظير عظاءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خطوات keeps its wāw because it is not a plural of فعل or feminine فعلة on فعل; heavy pluralization is avoided when it would add weight.
rows.anchor: ألا تراهم قالوا خطوات فلم يقلبوا الواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although قياس would give heavier plurals such as كلوات or جريات, speakers avoid them; yāʾ with kasra patterns like wāw with damma because both involve the same articulation.
rows.anchor: لأن الياء مع الكسرة كالواو مع الضمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فعللة from رميت follows فعلوة, yielding رميوة.
rows.anchor: وفعللة من رميت بمنزلة فعلوة رميوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In مثل ملكوت from رميت, the form is رموت; the dual is kept on the root pattern to distinguish it from the singular.
rows.anchor: وتقول في مثل ملكوت من رميت رموت ومن غزوت غزوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual رميا preserves the original shape to avoid confusing singular and dual; رحوي likewise remains unshortened to distinguish forms with different medial vowels.
rows.anchor: وقالوا رحوي ولم يحذفوا لأنهم لو حذفوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فوعلة and أفعلة from غزوت are غوزوة and أغزوة; فوعل is not غوزي because these nouns are built on the root, not on a derived verb form.
rows.anchor: وتقول في فوعلة من غزوت غوزوة وأفعلة أغزوة وفي فعل غزو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Building these nouns from augmented verbs would wrongly require forms such as غزواية, غوزية, or مغزي; their added pattern elements belong to the noun formation itself.
rows.anchor: وإنما بنيت هذا الاسم من غزوت من الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فوعلة and أفعلة from رميت are رومية and أرمية; the medial radical is kasra, by analogy with forms such as ثدي.
rows.anchor: وتقول في فوعلة من رميت رومية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu al-Khattab heard هبي and هبية; this supports keeping the pattern light rather than introducing an original movement that would produce heavier forms.
rows.anchor: وحدثنا أبو الخطاب أنه سمعهم يقولون هبي وهبية للصبي والصبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فعلالة from غزوت is غزواوة when not based on فعلال; where the latter base applies the form is غزواءة, not غزواية.
rows.anchor: وتقول في فعلالة من غزوت غزواوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forms like كوألل from رميت, غزوت, قويت, حييت, and شويت are built as روميا, غوزوا, قووا, حويا, and شويا; a quiescent wāw changes.
rows.anchor: وتقول في مثل كوألل من رميت روميا ومن غزوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فعول from غزوت is غزوو rather than غزي because the preceding fatḥa does not trigger the change found after kasra or damma.
rows.anchor: وتقول في فعول من غزوت غزوو لا تجعلها ياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In كعثول from قويت and شويت, the wāw changes to yāʾ, giving قيو and شي, as in the analogous form سيد.
rows.anchor: ولكنك قلبت الواو ياء كما قلبتها في سيد وهي من شويت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خلفنة from رميت and غزوت is رمينة and غزونة without further change because its original pattern has sukūn.
rows.anchor: لأن أصلها السكون فصارتا بمنزلة غزون ورمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The patterns صمحمح and جلبلاب yield رميما, رميماء, and غزيزاء; a quiescent wāw after kasra changes to yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وتقول في مثل صمحمح من رميت رميما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فوعلة from أعطيت is عوطوة on the root عطوت; the first and final radicals follow the corresponding positions in وعيت, رميت, and خشيت.
rows.anchor: عوطوة على الأصل لأنها من عطوت فأجر أول وعيت على أول وعدت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فعلية from غزوت and رميت gives غزوية and رميية, with the yāʾ either concealed or pronounced; it follows sound-root patterns like قعدد.
rows.anchor: وتقول في فعلية من غزوت غزوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فعل from غزوت is غز; substitution is obligatory after damma, as in محنية.
rows.anchor: وتقول في فعل من غزوت غز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فعلوة from غزوت is غزوية, not غزووة: the preceding vowel and doubled wāw conditions determine whether the first wāw behaves as a sound radical.
rows.anchor: ولا تقول غزووة لأنك إذا قلت عرقوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فيعلى from غزوت is غيزوي because the noun is built on that pattern rather than by adding the alif of duality to فيعل.
rows.anchor: وتقول في مثل فيعلي من غزوت غيزوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Geminate verbs can lose the first doubled consonant in forms whose final radical is fixed in sukūn and cannot receive movement, as in أحست and أحسن; the regular forms are أحسست and أحسسن.
rows.anchor: وذلك قولهم أحست يريدون أحسست وأحسن يريدون أحسسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the final radical can receive inflectional movement, contraction is avoided: لم أحس retains the geminate structure because the final position can be vocalized.
rows.anchor: تحذف لأن اللام في موضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fuller geminate forms أحسست, مسست, and ظللت are the common Arabic originals; ظلت and مست are exceptional contractions modeled on لست.
rows.anchor: وأما الذين قالوا ظلت ومست فشبهوها بلست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾanic forms مدت and حقت exemplify geminate verbs in this discussion of contraction.
rows.anchor: ولا نعلم شيئا من المضاعف شذ عما وصفت لك إلا هذه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A regular dialect treats فعل from رددت like فعل from قلت, producing قد رد and related forms; when عين is made quiescent its vowel moves onto the first radical.
rows.anchor: قد رد وهد ورحبت بلادك وظلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some speakers use an imāla-like signal in قد رد to show that a kasra has disappeared; similar vowel coloring marks the original damma in أغزي.
rows.anchor: وقد قال قوم قد رد فأمالوا الفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رد is the more frequent and better form; قيل, بيع, and خيف are more analogical because their first radicals are not treated as in the geminate past forms.
rows.anchor: لا يغير الإدغام المتحرك كما لا يغيره في فعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In forms such as تغزين, ishām is required: speakers avoid the severe loss of the original damma and wāw when weak-verb morphology changes the form.
rows.anchor: وأما تغزين ونحوها فالإشمام لازم لها ولنحوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the nominal pattern فعل from رددت, Sībawayh keeps the two radicals separate as ردد because that pattern does not occur as فعل.
rows.anchor: تقول في فعل من رددت ردد كما أخرجت فعلا على الأصل لأنه لا يكون فعلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two فعلان patterns from رددت are رددان; the source form is kept like a verbal noun without an added suffix.
rows.anchor: وتقول في فعلان رددان وفعلان رددان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For فعلان and its parallel pattern, the forms are ردان; each is treated as a three-letter base without following material, like فعل and فعل.
rows.anchor: وتقول في فعلان ردان وفعلان ردان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فعلول and فعليل from رددت are رددود and ردديد, preserving the doubled radicals as in the analogous فعلان forms.
rows.anchor: وتقول في فعلول من رددت رددود وفعليل ردديد كما فعلت ذلك بفعلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فعلان from قلت is قولان, treated like related sound-root patterns rather than like a geminate; the added material restores the original form.
rows.anchor: وأما فعلان من قلت فقولان كما فعلت ذلك بفعلان لأنها من غزوت لا تسكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: افعللت from رددت is اردددت; its last two radicals behave like the doubled final radicals of احمررت, and its verbal noun is ارددادا.
rows.anchor: وتقول في افعللت من رددت اردددت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A speaker who assimilates قتالا from الاقتتال also assimilates ارددادا, producing الرداد.
rows.anchor: ومن قال في الاقتتال قتالا فأدغم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: افعاللت from رددت is ارداددت, patterned after اشهاببت, with its first radical aligned to the pattern's first added consonant.
rows.anchor: وتقول في افعاللت ارداددت وتجريه مجرى اشهاببت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On مثل عثوثل, the form from ردد is ردودد because that pattern is an extension of سفرجل.
rows.anchor: وتقول في مثل عثوثل ردودد لأنه ملحق بسفرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: افعوعل and افعوعلت from ردد give اردود, يردود, and اردوددت; they follow احمررت in assimilation because no four-letter counterpart exists.
rows.anchor: قلت اردود يردود مثل يسبطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اقعنسس from ردد is اردندد, with the first radical aligned to عين and the two final radicals to سينسين.
rows.anchor: وتقول في مثل اقعنسس اردندد والأولى كالعين والأخريان كالسينين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In patterns such as دخلل and صمحمح, gemination is preserved; the final pair is not assimilated when doing so would recreate the structure being avoided.
rows.anchor: وفي مثل صمحمح رددد لأنه مثل سفرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جلعلع likewise keeps the final consonant unassimilated, preserving the root form rather than returning to the pattern speakers avoid.
rows.anchor: وتقول في مثل جلعلع رددد ولم تدغم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خلفنة from ردد is رددنة and is not assimilated because the consonant cannot receive movement, as in رددت.
rows.anchor: وتقول في مثل خلفنة رددنة لا تدغم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In patterns such as فوعل and فيعل, nouns and verbs retain the extended consonant sequence to preserve the pattern's weight, as with جلبب.
rows.anchor: اسما وإن كان فعلا قلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Keeping the extended pattern distinguishes forms attached to four- and five-letter measures from forms that are not attached to them.
rows.anchor: وإنما دعاهم إلى التسليم أن يفرقوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form ألندد supports treating the pattern as five-letter; its added nūn does not normally attach in this position except to extend a measure.
rows.anchor: ويقوي روددا ونحوه قولهم ألندد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Assimilation can occur even when one of the doubled letters is added, as in احمر and اطمأن; an extra radical does not itself block it.
rows.anchor: فإن قلت أقول جلب ورود لأن إحدى اللامين زائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فعول from ردد is ردود without assimilation because a vowel separates the two doubled consonants.
rows.anchor: ولا تشديد لأنك قد فصلت بينهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh lists exceptional weak forms such as ضيون, حيوة, and تهلل, alongside a quoted anonymous line; these preserve shapes otherwise treated as weak or irregular.
rows.anchor: وذلك نحو ضيون وقولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic has sound and weak patterns, and the regular weak forms follow the same principles as corresponding sound-root forms described earlier.
rows.anchor: العرب صحيحة ومعتلة وما قيس من معتله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some patterns are scarce or omitted because Arabic speakers avoid accumulating heavy gemination; forms of ردد may be used or dropped for that reason.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الشيء قد يقل في كلامهم وقد يتكلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even lighter doubled forms such as سلس and قلق can remain rare to prevent too many geminates; the scarcity of one pattern balances another.
rows.anchor: فمما قل فعلل وفعلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pattern may be omitted despite a heavier counterpart: وعوت and حيوت are avoided, while حييت, حيي, and even احووى occur; adjacent weak radicals are disliked.
rows.anchor: وقد يطرحون الشيء وغيره أثقل منه في كلامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other sparse forms include ددن and يديت.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الشيء قد يقل في كلامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pattern may be left unbuilt even where a similar form exists elsewhere: رشاء lacks a plural on فعل, and the corresponding weak pattern is omitted too.
rows.anchor: وقد يدعون البناء من الشيء قد يتكلمون بمثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nouns may occur on patterns omitted from verbs; Sībawayh says this and the other departures from the root pattern have been discussed above.
rows.anchor: اطرح من الفعل وقد بينا ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh closes by summarizing the behavior of sound and weak Arabic forms, including both regular and irregular patterns.
rows.anchor: على غير أصله وما يجئ على أصله بعلله
